domain_symbols.symbolic: symbolic expressions used by this domain

rules.name: RSA key generation correctness
rules.input_form: primes p, q; e with gcd(e, phi(n)) = 1; n = p*q
rules.output_form: d = e^{-1} mod phi(n); for all m < n, (m^e)^d == m mod n
rules.operation: Construct RSA keypair so encryption and decryption are mutual inverses by Euler's theorem.
counterexamples: Reusing primes across keys leaks private keys via gcd
common_errors: Using textbook RSA without OAEP padding allows chosen-ciphertext attacks

rules.name: Discrete log problem hardness
rules.input_form: cyclic group G of prime order q, generator g, element h = g^x
rules.output_form: computing x is conjectured hard in well-chosen G
preconditions: No known subexponential algorithm for chosen G
rules.operation: Underpin Diffie-Hellman and ECC by the assumed hardness of recovering x from g^x.
examples: Elliptic curve groups over finite fields with secure parameters
counterexamples: Multiplicative groups of finite fields have subexponential index-calculus attacks
common_errors: Using groups of smooth order vulnerable to Pohlig-Hellman

rules.name: Elliptic curve point doubling
rules.input_form: P = (x1, y1) on y^2 = x^3 + a x + b over F_p, y1 != 0
rules.output_form: lambda = (3 x1^2 + a)/(2 y1); x3 = lambda^2 - 2 x1; y3 = lambda (x1 - x3) - y1
preconditions: p prime, 4 a^3 + 27 b^2 != 0 mod p
rules.operation: Compute 2P on a Weierstrass elliptic curve using the tangent-line construction.
examples: Used in ECDSA, ECDH on curves like secp256k1, P-256, Curve25519
counterexamples: Singular curves do not form groups
common_errors: Not handling y1 = 0 case (point of order 2)

rules.name: Diffie-Hellman shared secret
rules.input_form: Alice's a, Bob's b in cyclic group G with generator g
rules.output_form: shared K = g^{ab}; Alice computes (g^b)^a, Bob computes (g^a)^b
preconditions: Authenticated public keys, large prime-order subgroup
rules.operation: Establish a shared secret over a public channel under DDH/CDH hardness.
common_errors: Using small subgroup elements, leaking partial bits of secret

rules.name: AES round structure
rules.operation: Apply substitution-permutation network rounds for symmetric block encryption.
examples: AES-GCM is the NIST-recommended AEAD mode
common_errors: Reusing nonces in GCM breaks confidentiality and authenticity

rules.name: Cryptographic hash collision resistance
rules.output_form: infeasible to find x != y with H(x) = H(y) in expected work much less than 2^{n/2}
rules.operation: Define collision resistance against the birthday attack baseline.
counterexamples: MD5 and SHA-1 have practical collisions
common_errors: Treating length-extension-prone constructions like MAC = H(key || msg) as secure

rules.name: Learning with errors (LWE)
rules.input_form: secret s, public (A, b = A s + e mod q) with small e
rules.output_form: recovering s is conjectured hard, even for quantum adversaries
preconditions: e drawn from narrow error distribution; A uniform
rules.operation: Base lattice-based cryptography on the conjectured hardness of LWE.
counterexamples: Too-small modulus or error allows linear algebra attacks
common_errors: Choosing error distribution outside provably-hard parameter regimes

rules.name: Shamir secret sharing
rules.input_form: secret s in F_q, threshold t, n shares
rules.output_form: polynomial f of degree t-1 with f(0) = s; shares (i, f(i))_{i=1..n}
rules.operation: Distribute a secret so any t shares reconstruct it via Lagrange interpolation and fewer reveal nothing.
examples: Used in threshold signatures, MPC, key escrow
counterexamples: t-1 shares give zero information about s (uniform marginal)

rules.name: Schnorr signature
rules.input_form: private x, public X = g^x, message m
rules.output_form: r = g^k; e = H(X, r, m); s = k - x e; signature (r, s)
rules.operation: Produce a Fiat-Shamir signature provably secure under DL in the ROM.
examples: Used in Bitcoin Taproot, MuSig2 threshold signatures
counterexamples: Nonce reuse leaks the private key
common_errors: Deterministic nonce without proper RFC 6979-style hashing

rules.name: Zero-knowledge soundness/completeness
rules.input_form: interactive protocol (P, V) for language L
rules.output_form: completeness: x in L => Pr[V accepts] >= 1-negl; soundness: x not in L => Pr[V accepts] <= negl
rules.operation: Define correctness of interactive proofs and arguments.
counterexamples: Witness-indistinguishability is strictly weaker than ZK

rules.name: GHZ-style commitment binding
rules.output_form: binding: hard to find m != m' opening same c; hiding: c reveals nothing about m
preconditions: At least computationally hard one-way function
rules.operation: Specify the two security properties any commitment scheme must satisfy.
examples: Pedersen commitments are perfectly hiding and computationally binding
counterexamples: Cannot simultaneously achieve perfect hiding and perfect binding
common_errors: Treating a hash H(m) alone as hiding for low-entropy messages

rules.name: Quantum-safe migration timeline
rules.input_form: current PKI using RSA/ECC; CRQC arrival time T
rules.output_form: data with confidentiality lifetime > T at risk now due to harvest-now-decrypt-later
rules.operation: Justify migrating long-lived secrets to hybrid PQC immediately even before CRQC exists.
examples: NIST PQC standards (Kyber, Dilithium, SPHINCS+, Falcon)
counterexamples: Symmetric AES-256 is widely considered quantum-safe
common_errors: Treating PQC migration as a future-only concern
